apps.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
apps.tagline: Expose local services to the internet securely via Cloudflare
apps.description: Cloudflare Tunnel creates a secure outbound connection from your server to Cloudflare's network — no inbound firewall rules or public IPs needed. Get your tunnel token from the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard.
apps.compose:
services:
  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run --token ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}

env.label: Tunnel Token
env.description: Found in Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard → Networks → Tunnels → your tunnel → Configure → Install connector.

apps.name: WireGuard Easy
apps.tagline: WireGuard VPN with a simple web UI
apps.description:
WG-Easy is the easiest way to run WireGuard VPN + a web UI for managing peers. Requires your server's public IP or hostname and a password hash.

Generate password hash on your server:
  docker run --rm ghcr.io/wg-easy/wg-easy:15 wgpw 'your-password'
apps.compose:
services:
  wg-easy:
    image: ghcr.io/wg-easy/wg-easy:15
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - WG_HOST=${WG_HOST}
      - WG_PORT=${WG_PORT}
      - WG_DEFAULT_DNS=${WG_DEFAULT_DNS}
    ports:
      - "${WG_PORT}:${WG_PORT}/udp"
      - "${WEBUI_PORT}:51821/tcp"
    volumes:
      - wg_data:/etc/wireguard
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
      - SYS_MODULE
    sysctls:
      - net.ipv4.conf.all.src_valid_mark=1
      - net.ipv4.ip_forward=1

volumes:
  wg_data:

env.label: Public Host
env.description: Public IP address or hostname of your server. Clients use this to connect.

env.label: WireGuard Port (UDP)
env.description: UDP port WireGuard listens on. Must be open in your firewall.

env.label: Web UI Port
env.description: Host port to expose the WG-Easy web UI on.

env.label: Default DNS
env.description: DNS server pushed to VPN clients.

apps.name: Nginx Proxy Manager
apps.tagline: Reverse proxy with SSL termination and a beautiful web UI
apps.description:
Nginx Proxy Manager makes it easy to forward traffic to your services with free SSL certificates from Let's Encrypt — no Nginx config files needed. Manage proxy hosts, redirections, 404 hosts, and stream hosts from a clean web dashboard.

Default admin credentials on first run:
  Email:    admin@example.com
  Password: changeme

Change them immediately after first login. Ports 80 and 443 must be available on the host for SSL certificate renewal and HTTPS termination to work.
apps.compose:
services:
  nginx-proxy-manager:
    image: jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      - "${ADMIN_PORT}:81"
    volumes:
      - npm_data:/data
      - npm_letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt

volumes:
  npm_data:
  npm_letsencrypt:

env.label: Admin UI Port
env.description: Host port for the Nginx Proxy Manager web dashboard.

apps.name: MySQL
apps.tagline: The world's most popular open-source relational database
apps.description:
MySQL is a battle-tested open-source relational database used by millions of applications worldwide. This setup runs MySQL 8 with a named volume for persistent data and exposes the standard port for external client connections.

Connect with any MySQL client using the credentials you set below. The root password is required; the app database and user are optional convenience defaults.
apps.compose:
services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:3306"
    environment:
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=${ROOT_PASSWORD}
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=${DB_NAME}
      - MYSQL_USER=${DB_USER}
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - mysql_data:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  mysql_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose MySQL on.

env.label: Root Password
env.description: Password for the MySQL root user. Use a strong random string.

env.label: Default Database
env.description: Name of the initial database to create.

env.label: Database User
env.description: Name of the initial non-root user.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the initial database user.

apps.name: MariaDB
apps.tagline: Community-developed MySQL-compatible relational database
apps.description:
MariaDB is a drop-in replacement for MySQL, developed by the original MySQL team. It offers improved performance, additional storage engines, and an active open-source community.

Fully compatible with MySQL clients and most MySQL applications. Use the same port and credentials format as MySQL.
apps.compose:
services:
  mariadb:
    image: mariadb:11
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:3306"
    environment:
      - MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=${ROOT_PASSWORD}
      - MARIADB_DATABASE=${DB_NAME}
      - MARIADB_USER=${DB_USER}
      - MARIADB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - mariadb_data:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  mariadb_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose MariaDB on.

env.label: Root Password
env.description: Password for the MariaDB root user.

env.label: Default Database
env.description: Name of the initial database to create.

env.label: Database User
env.description: Name of the initial non-root user.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the initial database user.

apps.name: PostgreSQL
apps.tagline: Advanced open-source object-relational database
apps.description:
PostgreSQL is a powerful, standards-compliant relational database with advanced features like JSONB, full-text search, window functions, CTEs, and extensive indexing options.

Connect with any PostgreSQL client (e.g. psql, pgAdmin, DBeaver) using the credentials below.
apps.compose:
services:
  postgresql:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:5432"
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=${DB_NAME}
      - POSTGRES_USER=${DB_USER}
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - postgresql_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  postgresql_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose PostgreSQL on.

env.label: Database Name
env.description: Name of the default database.

env.label: Database User
env.description: Name of the superuser.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the database user. Use a strong random string.

apps.name: Redis
apps.tagline: In-memory data store for caching, queues, and pub/sub
apps.description:
Redis is an ultra-fast in-memory data structure store used as a cache, message broker, session store, and real-time leaderboard backend. This setup uses the Alpine image with persistent AOF logging and optional password authentication.

Leave the password blank to run without authentication (suitable for private networks only).
apps.compose:
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:6379"
    command: >-
      redis-server
      --appendonly yes
      ${REDIS_PASSWORD:+--requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD}}
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data

volumes:
  redis_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Redis on.

env.label: Password
env.description: Optional password for Redis AUTH. Leave blank to disable authentication (only safe on private networks).

apps.name: MongoDB
apps.tagline: Document-oriented NoSQL database for flexible data models
apps.description:
MongoDB is a leading NoSQL database that stores data as flexible JSON-like documents instead of rows and columns. Ideal for applications with evolving schemas, hierarchical data, or high write throughput.

Connect with any MongoDB client (e.g. mongosh, MongoDB Compass) using the credentials below.
apps.compose:
services:
  mongodb:
    image: mongo:7
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:27017"
    environment:
      - MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME=${ROOT_USER}
      - MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD=${ROOT_PASSWORD}
      - MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE=${DB_NAME}
    volumes:
      - mongodb_data:/data/db

volumes:
  mongodb_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose MongoDB on.

env.label: Root Username
env.description: Username for the MongoDB root user.

env.label: Root Password
env.description: Password for the MongoDB root user. Use a strong random string.

env.label: Initial Database
env.description: Name of the initial database to create.

apps.name: Adminer
apps.tagline: Full-featured database management UI in a single container
apps.description:
Adminer is a lightweight, single-file database management tool that supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle, Elasticsearch, and more — all from one container.

Navigate to the web UI and enter your database host, credentials, and database name to connect. When connecting to another Docker service, use the service name as the host.
apps.compose:
services:
  adminer:
    image: adminer:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8080"

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Adminer web UI on.

apps.name: phpMyAdmin
apps.tagline: Web-based MySQL and MariaDB administration tool
apps.description:
phpMyAdmin is the most widely used web interface for managing MySQL and MariaDB databases. Browse tables, run queries, import/export data, and manage users from your browser.

Set the MySQL host to the service name or IP of your MySQL/MariaDB container. When running alongside another Docker Compose service, use the service name as the host.

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose phpMyAdmin on.

env.label: MySQL Host
env.description: Hostname or IP of your MySQL/MariaDB server. Use the Docker service name when on the same network.

env.label: MySQL Port
env.description: Port your MySQL/MariaDB server is listening on.

env.label: MySQL Root Password
env.description: Root password of your MySQL/MariaDB server. Used to allow root login via phpMyAdmin.

apps.name: pgAdmin 4
apps.tagline: Feature-rich web interface for managing PostgreSQL databases
apps.description:
pgAdmin 4 is the leading open-source management and administration tool for PostgreSQL. Query editor with syntax highlighting, ERD diagrams, server monitoring, backup/restore, and much more.

Log in with the email and password you set below. Then right-click Servers → Register → Server and enter your PostgreSQL connection details.
apps.compose:
services:
  pgadmin:
    image: dpage/pgadmin4:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    environment:
      - PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL=${ADMIN_EMAIL}
      - PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - pgadmin_data:/var/lib/pgadmin

volumes:
  pgadmin_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose pgAdmin on.

env.label: Admin Email
env.description: Email address used to log in to pgAdmin.

env.label: Admin Password
env.description: Password for the pgAdmin admin account. Use a strong password.

apps.name: MinIO
apps.tagline: High-performance S3-compatible self-hosted object storage
apps.description:
MinIO is a high-performance, Kubernetes-native object storage system that is API-compatible with Amazon S3. Use it for storing files, backups, ML datasets, and media — with the same SDK and tooling as AWS S3.

After installing, open the console and create buckets and access keys. Use the API port (9000) for S3-compatible clients and the console port (9001) for the web UI.
apps.compose:
services:
  minio:
    image: minio/minio:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    ports:
      - "${API_PORT}:9000"
      - "${CONSOLE_PORT}:9001"
    environment:
      - MINIO_ROOT_USER=${ROOT_USER}
      - MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=${ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data

volumes:
  minio_data:

env.label: API Port
env.description: Host port for the S3-compatible API endpoint. Point your S3 clients here.

env.label: Console Port
env.description: Host port for the MinIO web console.

env.label: Root User
env.description: Username for the MinIO root account (acts as AWS Access Key ID).

env.label: Root Password
env.description: Password for the MinIO root account (acts as AWS Secret Access Key). Minimum 8 characters.

apps.name: Nextcloud
apps.tagline: Self-hosted productivity platform — files, calendar, contacts, and more
apps.description:
Nextcloud is the most popular self-hosted cloud platform. It replaces Google Drive, Dropbox, Google Calendar, Contacts, and more — all running on your own server with full control of your data.

After installing, complete the setup wizard in the browser to create your admin account and configure the database. The bundled MariaDB handles data storage.
apps.compose:
services:
  nextcloud:
    image: nextcloud:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    environment:
      - MYSQL_HOST=db
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=nextcloud
      - MYSQL_USER=nextcloud
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER=${ADMIN_USER}
      - NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - nextcloud_data:/var/www/html
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: mariadb:11
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      - MARIADB_DATABASE=nextcloud
      - MARIADB_USER=nextcloud
      - MARIADB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - nextcloud_db:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  nextcloud_data:
  nextcloud_db:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Nextcloud on.

env.label: Admin Username
env.description: Username for the initial Nextcloud admin account.

env.label: Admin Password
env.description: Password for the initial Nextcloud admin account.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the internal MariaDB nextcloud user. Use a strong random string.

env.label: Database Root Password
env.description: Root password for the internal MariaDB instance.

apps.name: File Browser
apps.tagline: Web-based file manager for your server's filesystem
apps.description:
File Browser provides a web interface for browsing, uploading, downloading, editing, and managing files on your server. Supports user management, sharing links, and basic file operations.

Default credentials on first run: admin / admin — change them immediately in Settings.
apps.compose:
services:
  filebrowser:
    image: filebrowser/filebrowser:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    volumes:
      - ${ROOT_PATH}:/srv
      - filebrowser_data:/database

volumes:
  filebrowser_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose File Browser on.

env.label: Root Path
env.description: Host path to expose as the root directory in File Browser. Use / to browse the entire server filesystem.

apps.name: Grafana
apps.tagline: Open-source analytics and monitoring dashboards
apps.description:
Grafana is the most widely used open-source platform for monitoring and observability. Connect it to Prometheus, InfluxDB, Loki, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and 50+ other data sources to build beautiful dashboards and alerts.

Default credentials: admin / admin — you will be prompted to change the password on first login.
apps.compose:
services:
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=${ADMIN_USER}
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana

volumes:
  grafana_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Grafana on.

env.label: Admin Username
env.description: Username for the Grafana admin account.

env.label: Admin Password
env.description: Password for the Grafana admin account. Change this after first login.

apps.name: Prometheus
apps.tagline: Metrics collection and alerting system for infrastructure monitoring
apps.description:
Prometheus is an open-source monitoring system that collects and stores time-series metrics from configured targets. It pairs naturally with Grafana for visualization and Alertmanager for notifications.

After installing, edit the prometheus.yml config file in the data volume to add your scrape targets (e.g. node_exporter, cAdvisor, your apps).
apps.compose:
services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:9090"
    volumes:
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=${RETENTION}'

volumes:
  prometheus_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Prometheus web UI and API on.

env.label: Data Retention
env.description: How long to keep metrics data (e.g. 15d, 30d). Older data is automatically pruned.

apps.name: Beszel
apps.tagline: Lightweight server and Docker monitoring hub
apps.description: Beszel is a lightweight server monitoring platform with a web UI for tracking CPU, memory, disk, and Docker container stats across multiple systems.
apps.compose:
services:
  beszel:
    image: henrygd/beszel:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - APP_URL=${APP_URL}
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8090"
    volumes:
      - beszel_data:/beszel_data

volumes:
  beszel_data:

env.label: App URL
env.description: The URL you will use to access Beszel (e.g. http://your-server-ip:8090 or your domain).

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Beszel web UI on.

apps.name: Uptime Kuma
apps.tagline: Self-hosted uptime monitoring tool with a fancy UI
apps.description: Uptime Kuma is an easy-to-use self-hosted monitoring tool for tracking uptime of websites, TCP ports, DNS, and more with notifications support.
apps.compose:
services:
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data

volumes:
  uptime_kuma_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Uptime Kuma web UI on.

apps.name: MySpeed
apps.tagline: Self-hosted internet speed test tracker
apps.description: MySpeed saves your internet speed test results over time so you can track performance trends, detect outages, and monitor your ISP's reliability — all from a clean self-hosted dashboard.
apps.compose:
services:
  myspeed:
    image: germannewsmaker/myspeed:latest
    container_name: myspeed
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:5216"
    volumes:
      - myspeed_data:/myspeed/data

volumes:
  myspeed_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the MySpeed web UI on.

apps.name: Scrutiny
apps.tagline: Hard drive S.M.A.R.T. health monitoring with historical trends
apps.description:
Scrutiny monitors the S.M.A.R.T. health of all your hard drives and SSDs, surfacing failure predictions and historical trends in a clean web dashboard. The omnibus image bundles the web UI and InfluxDB time-series store in a single container.

After installing, add your disk devices to the compose file — by default /dev/sda is included. Add more entries (e.g. /dev/sdb, /dev/nvme0n1) as needed.
apps.compose:
services:
  scrutiny:
    image: ghcr.io/analogj/scrutiny:master-omnibus
    restart: unless-stopped
    cap_add:
      - SYS_RAWIO
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8080"
      - "${INFLUXDB_PORT}:8086"
    volumes:
      - /run/udev:/run/udev:ro
      - scrutiny_config:/opt/scrutiny/config
      - scrutiny_influxdb:/opt/scrutiny/influxdb
    devices:
      - /dev/sda
      # Add more drives: /dev/sdb, /dev/nvme0n1, etc.

volumes:
  scrutiny_config:
  scrutiny_influxdb:

env.label: Web UI Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Scrutiny web UI on.

env.label: InfluxDB Port
env.description: Host port for the bundled InfluxDB instance. Only needed if you want direct InfluxDB access; otherwise leave at the default.

apps.name: Portainer CE
apps.tagline: Container management UI for Docker and Kubernetes
apps.description:
Portainer Community Edition is a lightweight management UI that lets you easily manage your Docker environments — containers, images, networks, volumes, and stacks — from a browser.

The agent service lets Portainer manage the local Docker socket. The web UI is exposed on the port you choose. On first run, create your admin account within 5 minutes or the instance will lock down.
apps.compose:
services:
  portainer:
    image: portainer/portainer-ce:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:9443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - portainer_data:/data

volumes:
  portainer_data:

env.label: HTTPS Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Portainer web UI on (HTTPS).

apps.name: Dockge
apps.tagline: Fancy self-hosted Docker Compose stack manager
apps.description:
Dockge is a modern, reactive Docker Compose stack manager with a clean UI. Manage your compose stacks, view real-time logs, start/stop services, and edit compose files — all from a single web interface.

Stacks are stored under the stacks path you configure. Each subfolder is treated as a separate compose project.
apps.compose:
services:
  dockge:
    image: louislam/dockge:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:5001"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - dockge_data:/app/data
      - ${STACKS_PATH}:/opt/stacks
    environment:
      - DOCKGE_STACKS_DIR=/opt/stacks

volumes:
  dockge_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Dockge web UI on.

env.label: Stacks Path
env.description: Host directory where compose stacks will be stored. Each subdirectory is a stack.

apps.name: Gitea
apps.tagline: Lightweight self-hosted Git service
apps.description:
Gitea is a painless, self-hosted Git platform with a GitHub-like interface. It supports repositories, issues, pull requests, wikis, project boards, CI/CD via Gitea Actions, and package registries — all in a single lightweight binary.

On first access, complete the installation wizard. The bundled PostgreSQL handles data storage.
apps.compose:
services:
  gitea:
    image: gitea/gitea:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_PORT}:3000"
      - "${SSH_PORT}:22"
    environment:
      - GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres
      - GITEA__database__HOST=db:5432
      - GITEA__database__NAME=gitea
      - GITEA__database__USER=gitea
      - GITEA__database__PASSWD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - gitea_data:/data
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=gitea
      - POSTGRES_USER=gitea
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - gitea_db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  gitea_data:
  gitea_db:

env.label: HTTP Port
env.description: Host port for the Gitea web UI.

env.label: SSH Port
env.description: Host port for Git SSH operations.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the internal PostgreSQL database. Use a strong random string.

apps.name: Code Server
apps.tagline: VS Code in the browser — code from anywhere
apps.description:
Code Server runs VS Code on a remote server and lets you access it from any browser. Install extensions, open terminals, edit files, and run debuggers — all remotely with full VS Code features.

Set a strong password to protect access. The workspace path is the host directory opened in the editor.
apps.compose:
services:
  code-server:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/code-server:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8443"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - PASSWORD=${PASSWORD}
      - SUDO_PASSWORD=${SUDO_PASSWORD}
      - DEFAULT_WORKSPACE=/workspace
    volumes:
      - code_server_config:/config
      - ${WORKSPACE_PATH}:/workspace

volumes:
  code_server_config:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Code Server on.

env.label: Password
env.description: Password required to access the Code Server UI. Use a strong password.

env.label: Sudo Password
env.description: Password for sudo access inside the Code Server terminal. Can match the main password.

env.label: Workspace Path
env.description: Host directory to open as the default workspace in VS Code.

apps.name: n8n
apps.tagline: Workflow automation with a visual editor and 400+ integrations
apps.description:
n8n is a powerful workflow automation tool with a node-based visual editor. Connect 400+ services — APIs, databases, messaging apps, cloud platforms — into automated workflows without writing code (or with code when needed).

After installing, open the web UI and create your first workflow. Set a strong encryption key and basic auth credentials for security.
apps.compose:
services:
  n8n:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:5678"
    environment:
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_ACTIVE=true
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER=${ADMIN_USER}
      - N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - WEBHOOK_URL=${WEBHOOK_URL}
    volumes:
      - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n

volumes:
  n8n_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose n8n on.

env.label: Admin Username
env.description: Username for basic auth protection.

env.label: Admin Password
env.description: Password for basic auth protection. Use a strong password.

env.label: Encryption Key
env.description: Secret key used to encrypt stored credentials. Use a long random string (e.g. openssl rand -hex 32). Required — do not change after setup.

env.label: Webhook URL
env.description: Public URL where n8n is accessible. Used to generate webhook URLs. Set to your domain if behind a reverse proxy.

apps.name: Jellyfin
apps.tagline: Free and open-source media server — stream your movies, music, and TV
apps.description:
Jellyfin is a free software media system that lets you manage and stream your personal media collection — movies, TV shows, music, photos, and live TV. No subscriptions, no tracking, no external servers.

Mount your media directories under /media in the compose file. On first run, complete the setup wizard to create your admin account and add your libraries.
apps.compose:
services:
  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8096"
    volumes:
      - jellyfin_config:/config
      - jellyfin_cache:/cache
      - ${MEDIA_PATH}:/media

volumes:
  jellyfin_config:
  jellyfin_cache:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Jellyfin on.

env.label: Media Path
env.description: Host directory containing your media files. Subdirectories (Movies, TV, Music) can be added as separate libraries.

apps.name: Navidrome
apps.tagline: Modern self-hosted music server compatible with Subsonic clients
apps.description:
Navidrome is a modern, lightweight music server and streamer. It's compatible with all Subsonic API clients (DSub, Symfonium, Ultrasonic, and more), so you can listen to your music library on any device.

Point it at your music library path. The web UI includes a built-in player; external apps connect via the Subsonic API on the same port.
apps.compose:
services:
  navidrome:
    image: deluan/navidrome:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:4533"
    environment:
      - ND_SCANSCHEDULE=1h
      - ND_LOGLEVEL=info
      - ND_SESSIONTIMEOUT=24h
    volumes:
      - navidrome_data:/data
      - ${MUSIC_PATH}:/music:ro

volumes:
  navidrome_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Navidrome on.

env.label: Music Library Path
env.description: Host directory containing your music files. Navidrome will scan and index all audio files here.

apps.name: WordPress
apps.tagline: The world's most popular CMS — powers 40% of the web
apps.description:
WordPress is the most widely used content management system in the world, powering everything from personal blogs to enterprise websites. This setup includes WordPress with a MySQL backend.

After installing, complete the WordPress installation wizard in your browser to create your admin account and configure your site.
apps.compose:
services:
  wordpress:
    image: wordpress:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    environment:
      - WORDPRESS_DB_HOST=db
      - WORDPRESS_DB_NAME=wordpress
      - WORDPRESS_DB_USER=wordpress
      - WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - wordpress_data:/var/www/html
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: mysql:8
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=wordpress
      - MYSQL_USER=wordpress
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - wordpress_db:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  wordpress_data:
  wordpress_db:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose WordPress on.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the WordPress database user. Use a strong random string.

env.label: Database Root Password
env.description: Root password for the internal MySQL instance.

apps.name: Ghost
apps.tagline: Modern open-source publishing platform for blogs and newsletters
apps.description:
Ghost is a powerful open-source publishing platform built for professional bloggers, independent creators, and media companies. Supports posts, pages, newsletters, memberships, and subscriptions.

After installing, visit /ghost to complete setup and create your admin account. Set the URL to the public address where Ghost will be accessible.
apps.compose:
services:
  ghost:
    image: ghost:5-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:2368"
    environment:
      - url=${SITE_URL}
      - database__client=mysql
      - database__connection__host=db
      - database__connection__user=ghost
      - database__connection__password=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - database__connection__database=ghost
    volumes:
      - ghost_data:/var/lib/ghost/content
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: mysql:8
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=ghost
      - MYSQL_USER=ghost
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ghost_db:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  ghost_data:
  ghost_db:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Ghost on.

env.label: Site URL
env.description: Public URL of your Ghost site. Used for links in emails and the admin panel. Update if behind a reverse proxy.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the Ghost database user.

env.label: Database Root Password
env.description: Root password for the internal MySQL instance.

apps.name: Vaultwarden
apps.tagline: Unofficial Bitwarden-compatible server — self-hosted password manager
apps.description:
Vaultwarden is an unofficial, lightweight Bitwarden-compatible server written in Rust. It's fully compatible with all official Bitwarden clients (browser extensions, mobile apps, desktop app) and uses a fraction of the resources of the official server.

After installing, register your account via the web vault or any Bitwarden client by pointing it at your Vaultwarden URL. Disable new registrations after creating your account (or use the admin token to manage users).
apps.compose:
services:
  vaultwarden:
    image: vaultwarden/server:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    environment:
      - DOMAIN=${DOMAIN}
      - ADMIN_TOKEN=${ADMIN_TOKEN}
      - SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=${SIGNUPS_ALLOWED}
    volumes:
      - vaultwarden_data:/data

volumes:
  vaultwarden_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Vaultwarden on.

env.label: Domain
env.description: Full public URL of your Vaultwarden instance. Required for WebAuthn and email links to work correctly.

env.label: Admin Token
env.description: Secret token to access the /admin panel. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 48. Leave blank to disable the admin panel.

env.label: Allow Signups
env.description: Set to 'false' to disable new user registration after you've created your account.

apps.name: Mattermost
apps.tagline: Open-source team messaging — a self-hosted Slack alternative
apps.description:
Mattermost is an open-source, self-hosted messaging platform for team communication. Channels, direct messages, file sharing, threaded replies, and integrations — all without sending your data to a third party.

After installing, complete the setup wizard to create the first admin account. The bundled PostgreSQL handles data storage.
apps.compose:
services:
  mattermost:
    image: mattermost/mattermost-team-edition:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8065"
    environment:
      - MM_SQLSETTINGS_DRIVERNAME=postgres
      - MM_SQLSETTINGS_DATASOURCE=postgres://mattermost:${DB_PASSWORD}@db:5432/mattermost?sslmode=disable
      - MM_SERVICESETTINGS_SITEURL=${SITE_URL}
    volumes:
      - mattermost_data:/mattermost/data
      - mattermost_logs:/mattermost/logs
      - mattermost_config:/mattermost/config
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=mattermost
      - POSTGRES_USER=mattermost
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - mattermost_db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  mattermost_data:
  mattermost_logs:
  mattermost_config:
  mattermost_db:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Mattermost on.

env.label: Site URL
env.description: Public-facing URL of your Mattermost instance. Update to your domain if behind a reverse proxy.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the internal PostgreSQL database. Use a strong random string.

apps.name: ntfy
apps.tagline: Simple HTTP-based pub/sub notification service
apps.description:
ntfy is a simple pub/sub notification service that lets you send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts, curl, or any HTTP client — no account or API key needed.

Subscribe to a topic in the ntfy app (Android/iOS) or web UI, then send notifications with a simple HTTP POST to your server. Enable auth below to restrict who can publish or subscribe.
apps.compose:
services:
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: serve
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"
    environment:
      - NTFY_BASE_URL=${BASE_URL}
      - NTFY_AUTH_DEFAULT_ACCESS=${DEFAULT_ACCESS}
    volumes:
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy

volumes:
  ntfy_data:
  ntfy_cache:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose ntfy on.

env.label: Base URL
env.description: Public URL of your ntfy server. Used in notification payloads and the web UI.

env.label: Default Access
env.description: Default access level for unauthenticated users: read-write, read-only, write-only, or deny-all.

apps.name: Memos
apps.tagline: Lightweight self-hosted note-taking app with markdown and tags
apps.description:
Memos is an open-source, privacy-focused note-taking application. Capture thoughts, ideas, and snippets in plain text or Markdown, tag them, and search across all your notes — with a Twitter-like timeline UI.

All notes are stored locally in a SQLite database. On first launch, create your admin account.
apps.compose:
services:
  memos:
    image: neosmemo/memos:stable
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:5230"
    volumes:
      - memos_data:/var/opt/memos

volumes:
  memos_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Memos on.

apps.name: Stirling PDF
apps.tagline: Self-hosted PDF manipulation tool with 50+ operations
apps.description:
Stirling PDF is a powerful, locally hosted web app for all your PDF needs. Merge, split, compress, convert, rotate, sign, watermark, and more — all processed on your server, never uploaded to third-party services.

No account needed. Just open the web UI and start working with your PDFs.
apps.compose:
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - stirling_pdf_data:/usr/share/tesseract-ocr/5/tessdata
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false

volumes:
  stirling_pdf_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose Stirling PDF on.

apps.name: IT Tools
apps.tagline: Collection of handy online tools for developers
apps.description:
IT Tools is a beautifully designed collection of developer utilities — converters, encoders, generators, formatters, and more — all running locally in your browser. No data leaves your server.

Includes tools for JWT decoding, UUID generation, hash computation, base64 encoding, color conversion, cron expression parsing, regex testing, text diffing, and dozens more.
apps.compose:
services:
  it-tools:
    image: corentinth/it-tools:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:80"

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose IT Tools on.

apps.name: Umami
apps.tagline: Privacy-first, self-hosted web analytics
apps.description:
Umami is a simple, fast, privacy-focused alternative to Google Analytics. No cookies, no personal data, GDPR compliant by design. Tracks page views, visitors, referrers, devices, and custom events.

After installing, open the web UI and log in with the default credentials (admin / umami) — change the password immediately. Then create a website to get your Website ID and tracking script.
apps.compose:
services:
  umami:
    image: ghcr.io/umami-software/umami:postgresql-latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:3000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://umami:${DB_PASSWORD}@db:5432/umami
      - DATABASE_TYPE=postgresql
      - APP_SECRET=${APP_SECRET}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=umami
      - POSTGRES_USER=umami
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - umami_db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U umami"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  umami_db:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Umami web UI on.

env.label: Database Password
env.description: Password for the internal PostgreSQL database. Use a strong random string.

env.label: App Secret
env.description: Random secret used to sign session tokens. Use a long random string.

apps.name: Open WebUI
apps.tagline: Self-hosted AI chat interface for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs
apps.description:
Open WebUI is a feature-rich, self-hosted web interface for interacting with large language models. Works out of the box with Ollama and supports any OpenAI-compatible API.

Features include multi-model chat, RAG document Q&A, image generation, voice input, user management, and full conversation history — all in a polished ChatGPT-style UI.

To connect a local Ollama instance set the Ollama URL below. To use OpenAI or another provider, leave Ollama URL blank and provide your API key.
apps.compose:
services:
  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8080"
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=${OLLAMA_BASE_URL}
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
    volumes:
      - open_webui_data:/app/backend/data

volumes:
  open_webui_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Open WebUI on.

env.label: Ollama URL
env.description: URL of your Ollama instance. Use http://host.docker.internal:11434 to reach Ollama running on the host machine. Leave blank if using an OpenAI-compatible API only.

env.label: OpenAI API Key
env.description: Optional. API key for OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible provider. Leave blank if using Ollama only.

env.label: Secret Key
env.description: Secret key used to sign session tokens. Use a long random string — required for production use.

apps.name: QwenPaw
apps.tagline: Self-hosted personal AI assistant with multi-agent, skills, and memory
apps.description:
QwenPaw is a self-hosted personal AI assistant built on Qwen models. Run it on your own server for full data control — memory, skills, and configuration never leave your machine.

Features multi-agent collaboration, extensible skills (scheduling, document processing, news digests), integrations with Telegram, Discord, WeChat, DingTalk, and Feishu, and persistent memory that evolves with use.

After installing, open the web console and configure your model provider API key in Settings → Model Provider. Enable authentication (recommended) via the environment variables below.
apps.compose:
services:
  qwenpaw:
    image: agentscope/qwenpaw:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:8088"
    environment:
      - QWENPAW_AUTH_ENABLED=${AUTH_ENABLED}
      - QWENPAW_AUTH_USERNAME=${AUTH_USERNAME}
      - QWENPAW_AUTH_PASSWORD=${AUTH_PASSWORD}
      - DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=${DASHSCOPE_API_KEY}
    volumes:
      - qwenpaw_data:/app/working
      - qwenpaw_secrets:/app/working.secret
      - qwenpaw_backups:/app/working.backups

volumes:
  qwenpaw_data:
  qwenpaw_secrets:
  qwenpaw_backups:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the QwenPaw web console on.

env.label: DashScope API Key
env.description: Alibaba Cloud DashScope API key for Qwen model access. Get one at dashscope.aliyun.com. You can also configure other model providers from the web console after install.

env.label: Enable Authentication
env.description: Set to 'true' to require login to access the web console. Recommended when exposing to a network.

env.label: Admin Username
env.description: Username for the web console login. Only used when authentication is enabled.

env.label: Admin Password
env.description: Password for the web console login. Use a strong password. Only used when authentication is enabled.

apps.name: 9Router
apps.tagline: Smart AI model router across 40+ providers with token compression and fallback
apps.description:
9Router is an open-source AI API gateway that intelligently routes requests across 40+ providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Cursor, and more) and 100+ models. Features automatic token compression to cut costs, multi-account round-robin load balancing, real-time quota tracking, and seamless format translation between different AI platforms — all behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

After installing, open the web UI and log in with the initial password. Then configure your provider API keys in the dashboard and point your apps at 9Router's endpoint.
apps.compose:
services:
  9router:
    image: decolua/9router:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:20128"
    environment:
      - DATA_DIR=/app/data
      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET}
      - INITIAL_PASSWORD=${INITIAL_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - 9router_data:/app/data

volumes:
  9router_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the 9Router web UI and API endpoint on.

env.label: JWT Secret
env.description: Secret key used to sign dashboard session tokens. Use a long random string — required for security.

env.label: Initial Password
env.description: Password for the first login to the web dashboard. Change it immediately after the first login.

apps.name: Hermes Agent
apps.tagline: Self-improving AI agent with memory, skills, and multi-platform messaging
apps.description:
Hermes Agent is a self-hosted personal AI assistant by Nous Research. It features a closed learning loop — it creates skills from experience, builds persistent memory across sessions, and runs scheduled automations. Connect any model (OpenAI, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and more) and talk to it via Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, or CLI.

After installing, open the dashboard and add your model provider API key in Settings. The gateway uses host networking for full connectivity; the dashboard is exposed on the port you choose below.
apps.compose:
services:
  gateway:
    image: nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
    container_name: hermes-gateway
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - hermes_data:/opt/data
    command: ["gateway", "run"]

  dashboard:
    image: nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
    container_name: hermes-dashboard
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:9119"
    depends_on:
      - gateway
    volumes:
      - hermes_data:/opt/data
    command: ["dashboard", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--no-open"]

volumes:
  hermes_data:

env.label: Dashboard Port
env.description: Host port to expose the Hermes dashboard on. Open this port in your firewall.

apps.name: OmniRoute
apps.tagline: Unified AI gateway for 160+ providers with smart routing and token compression
apps.description:
OmniRoute is an open-source AI API gateway that routes requests across 160+ providers (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Deepseek, Groq, and more) through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Features automatic prompt compression for 15–95% token reduction, multi-account round-robin load balancing, auto-fallback on provider errors, and real-time usage tracking — all managed from a built-in dashboard.

After installing, open the web UI, log in with your initial password, and add your provider API keys in Settings. Point your apps at OmniRoute's endpoint and select your routing strategy.
apps.compose:
services:
  omniroute:
    image: diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:20128"
    environment:
      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET}
      - API_KEY_SECRET=${API_KEY_SECRET}
      - INITIAL_PASSWORD=${INITIAL_PASSWORD}
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=${BASE_URL}
    volumes:
      - omniroute_data:/app/data

volumes:
  omniroute_data:

env.label: Port
env.description: Host port to expose the OmniRoute dashboard and API endpoint on.

env.label: JWT Secret
env.description: Secret key for signing dashboard session tokens. Use a long random string (e.g. openssl rand -base64 48).

env.label: API Key Secret
env.description: Encryption key for stored provider API keys. Use a 32-byte hex string (e.g. openssl rand -hex 32).

env.label: Initial Password
env.description: Password for the first dashboard login. Change it immediately after the first login.

env.label: Base URL
env.description: Public-facing URL where OmniRoute is accessible. Used for dashboard links and CORS. Update if behind a reverse proxy.
